slides.title: Attending to More Than Just the Words
bullets: Active listening attends to emphasis, hesitation and emotional undertone, not just content
Demonstrating that attention in a way that deepens rather than interrupts the conversation
The skill that makes exploratory and reflective questioning actually work

slides.title: Full Attention, Not the Next Talking Point
bullets: Genuinely focus on the speaker rather than preparing the next data point
A surprisingly common habit among MSLs confident in their scientific content
Treats conversation as a genuine exchange, not waiting for a turn to speak

slides.title: Non-Verbal Signals Matter Too
bullets: Appropriate eye contact and unhurried pacing
Not glancing at a phone or watch
Signals attention concretely, and its absence is noticed even when unintentional

slides.title: Withhold Judgment Before Responding
bullets: Resist the urge to immediately counter a concern with a data point
Paraphrasing and reflecting confirms understanding and invites elaboration
Creates space for a physician to finish a genuinely complex thought

slides.title: Listen for What Isn't Said
bullets: A shift in tone or vagueness communicates something real
Example: enthusiastic on efficacy, noticeably vaguer on tolerability
Skilled listening notices the shift and gently invites it into the open

slides.title: Better Listening, Better Insight Capture
bullets: Active listening improves the accuracy of insight summaries written afterward
MSLs who listen carefully track substance in the moment, not from memory later
A direct input into the quality of medical intelligence, not just a soft skill

takeaway.title: Active listening is what turns well-designed questions into real conversational value
bullets: Full attention, non-verbal engagement and withheld judgment are all learnable components
What a physician doesn't say is often as informative as what they do say
Careful listening in the moment produces more accurate insight afterward
